finding: The Act covers manufactured plant products; the narrower plant-material definition is not an exemption from the separate plant-product limb. Sections 25–26 require permits/certificates only where the applicable specification requires them. Section 27 is an affirmative advance written-application duty only for a type not already the subject of a specification. Current ministry-published PP29 (dried herbs) is no-permit/no-PC; PP23 (dried plant material) requires a permit. Those are genuinely competing general categories for finished infusion leaves, not merely absent literal tea naming.
proposedDecision: Keep unresolved. Conservative exclusion cannot be justified merely because the researcher has not demonstrated the specification: that is a verification standard, not the statutory section 27 trigger. If the complete register demonstrates no applicable specification, section 27 would justify no-doc exclusion; if PP29 covers finished Camellia leaves, the no-document route may be supportable.
newSourceResult: Recovered the complete 73-page Act directly from the current ministry Act-page link. Its PDF text layer uses faulty font encoding, while previously saved official IPPC text confirms the relevant provisions. Public WordPress media searches for import and tea returned 403; no alternate specification was retrieved and no access bypass attempted.
preciseRemainingEvidence: An applicable current specification or a general published meaning/category allocation that distinguishes PP29 dried herbs from PP23 dried plant material for manufactured infusion tea; alternatively an exhaustive register showing this type has no specification. No bespoke individual ruling is intrinsically necessary.
contraryInterpretation: A conservative operator could elect not to ship without demonstrated PP29 coverage. That is a business hold, not evidence that the law affirmatively requires every finished tea importer to make an application.
confidence: High for conditional statutory trigger and table text; classification remains unresolved.
